scoring_justification: The checker cannot re-run the heavy Monte Carlo simulations. It validates cubic symmetry of S matrices, recomputes directional Poisson's ratios from reported stiffness constants to cross-check internal consistency, and then compares the agent's PR_min (computed from those stiffness constants) against paper-derived auxeticity sign thresholds and isotropy monotonicity rules. This is a legitimate result-level comparison with hidden trends, not a full recompute from raw box trajectories.

hidden_assets.purpose: Expected auxeticity signs per system type and isotropy monotonicity rule, derived from the paper's reported trends and thresholds (Section 4, Figures 9-10).
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper 'Removing Auxetic Properties in f.c.c. Hard Sphere Crystals by Orthogonal Nanochannels' (Materials 2022, 15, 1134), specifically the text describing that for separate-channel layouts at p*=250, the minimum Poisson's ratio becomes non-negative (auxeticity removed) when sigma'/sigma > 1.01, while crossing layouts retain negative PR.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's explicit numerical statements. For separate-channel systems: PR_min < 0 at sigma'/sigma = 1.0 (pristine f.c.c. is auxetic), PR_min >= 0 for sigma'/sigma >= 1.025. For crossing-channel systems: PR_min < 0 for all studied ratios. Isotropy ratio for separate D-type channels must increase from sigma'/sigma=1.0 to 1.1.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These thresholds are directly stated in the published paper text and accompanying figures. A correct reproduction of the system must satisfy these physical trends, so the gold is grounded in the paper's own findings.

outputs.description: Elastic compliance and stiffness matrix elements and cubic symmetry flag for each simulated system.
Directional and extreme Poisson's ratios and isotropy ratio for each system, used to verify removal of auxetic properties and anisotropy trends.

output_contract.notes: The checker validates cubic symmetry of the reported compliance matrices and checks internal consistency between the reported Poisson's ratios and the stiffness matrix elements. The auxeticity condition (PR_min ≥ 0 for separate‑channel systems) is verified against expected behaviour.

steps.description: Verify that for each system, the elastic compliance matrix S satisfies cubic symmetry relations: |S11-S22|, |S11-S33|, |S44-S55|, |S44-S66|, |S12-S13|, |S12-S23| < 0.03, and other S max abs < 0.03.

Recompute directional Poisson's ratios from the B11, B12, B44 values stored in s_matrix_results.json and compare to the agent's reported values in pr_results.json. The absolute difference must be below 0.05.

Check that the reported minimum Poisson's ratio PR_min follows the paper's physical trend: for separate-channel systems, PR_min must be negative at sigma'/sigma=1.0 and non-negative at 1.025, 1.05, 1.075, 1.1; for crossing-channel systems, PR_min must be negative for all ratios. Each correctly classified system earns a fraction of the weight.
For separate D-type channels, the isotropy_ratio must increase from sigma'/sigma=1.0 to 1.1 (i.e., isotropy_ratio at 1.1 > isotropy_ratio at 1.0). Full credit if satisfied, zero otherwise.
